interest: This file offers valuable insight into the operational mechanisms of Axis civilian control and intelligence coordination in wartime Italy. Specifically, it provides documentary evidence of how overseas Japanese expatriate associations like the Roma Nippon Kurabu (Nipponjin-kai) operated under the aegis of the Japanese Embassy, conducting surveillance and passport checks on private Japanese citizens residing in Rome. Furthermore, the file demonstrates Allied intelligence exploitation of captured Axis materials in liberated Italy, showing the pipeline of intelligence gathered by the Commander Eighth Fleet's Naval Intelligence Unit, processed by the Office of Naval Intelligence (ONI), and shared across agencies with the State Department and the FBI. Lastly, the cross-reference note highlights the unusual diplomatic status of individuals serving dual Axis roles, such as the Japanese Honorary Consul in Naples who simultaneously worked as a German consular employee prior to his arrest in 1943.
overview: This file contains U.S. State Department records classified under decimal file 894.20265, concerning Japanese military activities, intelligence gathering, and espionage in Italy during World War II. The file consists of two primary items from late 1943 and 1944: a November 1943 cross-reference sheet regarding the arrest and internment of the Japanese Honorary Consul in Naples, who concurrently served as a minor German consular employee; and a September 1944 memorandum from the Office of the Chief of Naval Operations forwarding an Office of Naval Intelligence (ONI) translation to the Department of State. The translated May 1943 document from the Roma Nippon Kurabu (Casa del Giappone) in Rome illustrates the close collaboration between Japanese overseas civilian associations and diplomatic missions, specifically detailing the surveillance and passport checks conducted on Japanese residents in Italy.

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet noting the arrest in Naples of an honorary Japanese consul who was also a German consular employee, and requesting internment instructions.
subfiles.summary: This cross-reference sheet indexes telegram No. 1882 sent at 6 p.m. on November 1, 1943, by John C. Wiley in Algiers to the Department of State. It reports the arrest of the Japanese Honorary Consul in Naples, who was also employed as a minor German consular official. The document indicates that State Department instructions regarding the consul's internment were requested under file number 702.9465/1.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet on Arrest and Internment of Japanese Honorary Consul in Naples

subfiles.about: Cover memorandum transmitting an Office of Naval Intelligence translation concerning the activities of the Roma Nippon Kurabu.
subfiles.from: Wallace S. Wharton, Captain, U.S.N.R. (Office of the Chief of Naval Operations)
keywords: Office of the Chief of Naval Operations
subfiles.summary: Captain Wallace S. Wharton of the Office of the Chief of Naval Operations transmits an Office of Naval Intelligence translation dated September 22, 1944, to Frederick B. Lyon at the Department of State. The memorandum forwards intelligence on the activities of the Roma Nippon Kurabu in Rome, Italy, for Lyon's information and retention. It also notes that the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) was made cognizant of the matter.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Captain Wallace S. Wharton to Frederick B. Lyon regarding Roma Nippon Kurabu

subfiles.about: Office of Naval Intelligence translation of a captured 1943 letter from the Nippon Club in Rome submitting civilian surveillance and passport check reports to the Japanese Embassy.
subfiles.from: Office of Naval Intelligence / Commander Eighth Fleet, Naval Intelligence Unit
subfiles.summary: This translation prepared by the Office of Naval Intelligence translates a May 3, 1943 letter on Roma Nippon Kurabu (Casa del Giappone) stationery obtained by Commander Eighth Fleet's Naval Intelligence Unit in September 1944. The letter, addressed to the Japanese Embassy in Rome, transmits an investigative report in triplicate and an accompanying roster concerning a passport check of Japanese civilian residents. An ONI prefatory note underscores the document's significance in illustrating the close coordination between Japanese expatriate associations (Nipponjin-kai) and official diplomatic and consular authorities.
subfiles.title: Office of Naval Intelligence Translation: Roma Nippon Kurabu Activities and Passport Check
